name: Socialist democracy
summary: Socialist democracy holds that socialism and democracy are inseparable: political democracy, either multi-party representative or direct, must be complemented by economic democracy through social ownership and workers' control, as in cooperatives, councils, democratic unions and public enterprises. Its adherents reject one-party rule and the suppression of dissent, arguing that socialism cannot be decreed from above and needs open public life, free elections, press and assembly.
scope: The democratic strand described in Wikipedia's article: democratic socialists, Trotskyists, libertarian socialists and reformists who equate socialist democracy with political pluralism plus economic democracy, drawing on Rosa Luxemburg's critique of Bolshevism, Trotsky's call for Soviet democracy, and the SEP account of democratic socialism. It excludes the Marxist-Leninist usage in which the term denotes the one-party state, and the anarchist rejection of state power; it overlaps with the separately audited democratic socialism.

keyFigures.name: Rosa Luxemburg
keyFigures.role: Marxist theorist whose critique of Bolshevism defended democracy and freedom of dissent within socialism.

keyFigures.name: Leon Trotsky
keyFigures.role: Revolutionary who called for the revival of Soviet democracy and multiple Soviet parties against bureaucratic rule.

sources.title: Socialist democracy

sources.usedFor: Definitions of socialist democracy, the democratic versus Marxist-Leninist usages, economic democracy forms, and the debate on socialism and freedom.

sources.title: The Russian Revolution, ch. 6: The Problem of Dictatorship
sources.author: Rosa Luxemburg (1918)
sources.usedFor: Freedom for dissenters, general elections, free press and assembly, public control, rejection of party dictatorship.

sources.title: The Revolution Betrayed, ch. 11: Whither the Soviet Union?

sources.usedFor: Soviet democracy, revival of Soviet parties and trade unions, planning needing democracy, political revolution against bureaucracy.

sources.title: Socialism
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Social ownership, workplace democracy, market socialism versus planning, reform versus revolution, equality and domination.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Raising the pay floor follows from the aim of reducing capitalist inequality and worker domination, but the sources describe ownership and democratic control rather than wage law, so it is an implication.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The SEP entry shows socialists keeping markets only after removing the capitalist class and criticises capitalist inequality, so the claim that free markets beat government allocation is rejected.

public-ownership.rationale: The Wikipedia article names social ownership of production through state-owned enterprises, cooperatives and sovereign wealth funds as the economic half of socialist democracy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The SEP entry says capitalism concentrates wealth and political influence, so socialists favour curbing top fortunes; higher taxes are the usual means though not the sources' main topic.

unions-good.rationale: The Wikipedia article lists democratic trade unions among the standard forms of economic democracy, and Trotsky demands the resurrection of the trade unions as part of Soviet democracy.

property-fundamental.rationale: The SEP entry treats the bulk of productive property as properly under social control, so private property rights are not fundamental and may be overridden democratically.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Socialist democrats want democratic control over large firms and see corporate power as undermining democracy, so tighter regulation is a minimum position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare cuts contradict the egalitarian and anti-domination grounds that the SEP gives for socialist institutions; the dependency argument is a market-liberal one.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker-owned cooperatives and workers' councils are named in the Wikipedia article as central forms of economic democracy, and the SEP calls worker self-management a core socialist ideal.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Luxemburg demands unrestricted freedom of press and assembly, which points against speech restrictions, but many modern democratic socialists accept hate-speech laws, so this is a low-confidence lean.

strong-leader.rationale: Luxemburg denounces rule by a handful of politicians and "decreeing" socialism from behind official desks; a leader bypassing deliberation is the opposite of socialist democracy.

state-harmful.rationale: The article contrasts socialist democracy with anarchist rejection of the state: democratic socialists and Trotskyists use democratic state institutions, even if Trotsky expects the state to wither eventually.

decide-locally.rationale: The SEP entry covers both local participatory institutions such as Porto Alegre budgeting and national democratic planning, so adherents split between local and national decision making.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not covered in the sources; modern democratic socialist parties such as Die Linke and DSA support it, and the position follows equal rights, but the classical texts predate the issue.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a concern of the sources; socialist democracy is oriented to class and democracy more than national culture, an inference.

gradual-change.rationale: The SEP entry favours a combined strategy of reform and eroding capitalist power, while Luxemburg and Trotsky call for radical transformation; established institutions are respected only as democratic channels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The sources are silent, and adherents split between internationalist support and criticism of institutions like the EU and IMF as capitalist.

nation-first.rationale: Trotsky's internationalism and the working-class focus of the sources reject national self-interest over cooperation, though the sources do not treat the question directly.

open-borders.rationale: The sources are silent; internationalism favours free movement as an ideal, but many adherents hold more cautious positions today.

limit-growth.rationale: Not covered by the chosen sources; eco-socialists favour limits while other adherents favour growth with redistribution.

revolution-justified.rationale: Trotsky holds that the bureaucratic caste "can be removed only by a revolutionary force" and Luxemburg is a revolutionary, though reformist adherents prefer elections; revolution is justified but not usual.

experts-over-public.rationale: Luxemburg wants the masses to take part in public life and not have socialism decreed by officials, and Trotsky wants a democracy of producers and consumers, so rule by experts is rejected.

central-planning.rationale: The SEP entry notes central planning's information and power problems while Trotsky defends the planned economy under democracy; adherents split between market socialists and democratic planners.

socialized-markets.rationale: The SEP entry describes market socialism with worker or publicly owned firms as a main model of economic democracy, and the Wikipedia article cites Yugoslav self-management, though planners disagree.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Curbing inherited wealth follows from the egalitarian and anti-domination case for socialist institutions that the SEP discusses, though it names no tax.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Democratic planning or public steering of investment follows from social ownership of the bulk of productive assets in the SEP account, though market socialists prefer less direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The SEP entry puts the focus on social or collective ownership of productive assets, not on small owners; this is a distributist position socialists generally do not hold.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Trotsky notes the state's withering is a long process and accepts a transitional economy with wages, while the sources do not treat abolition of wages as a programme item.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Leaving money to the market contradicts social control of the economy, which the SEP treats as definitional.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The sources describe democratic unions and councils rather than state-recognized bargaining bodies; some social-democratic adherents accept it, so this is a lean.

one-party-rule.rationale: Luxemburg argues that freedom only for supporters of one party is no freedom and Trotsky calls for the revival of Soviet parties, while the Wikipedia article contrasts this with the Marxist-Leninist use of the term.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Democracy is the defining element and the Wikipedia article's forms of socialist democracy are all elected, so hereditary rule is rejected.

democracy-best.rationale: The Wikipedia article states that democracy is a key component of most socialist schools and defines socialist democracy as a democratic system, and Luxemburg treats democracy as indispensable to socialism.

direct-votes.rationale: The article names direct democracy as one of two main meanings of socialist democracy, alongside multi-party representative democracy, so adherents split but lean to supporting direct input.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' councils are named as a form of economic democracy, but Luxemburg criticises replacing elected representative bodies with soviets, so adherents want councils alongside rather than instead of parliament.

natural-rulers.rationale: Luxemburg's insistence that the masses must take part in public life and be able to correct errors excludes the notion of naturally superior rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Trotsky holds that the bureaucracy can be removed only by revolutionary force, and the revolutionary strand does not renounce violence, though reformists in the current do.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing in the sources valorizes war, and the socialist tradition treats war as a product of capitalism and ruling-class rivalry.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Socialist democracy makes law the product of democratic decisions, so scriptural authority is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Social control of the economy and democratic public institutions rule out privatizing coercive public functions.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The tradition is built on class and democratic citizenship rather than ethnicity, so an ethnically defined nation is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Marxist strands in the Wikipedia article treat class conflict as the key to history, while liberal socialists like Mill and Dahl do not, so it is a majority view.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The SEP entry notes socialism's pursuit of broadly equal access to the means of participation and discusses equal-outcome approaches, though not all adherents demand strict equality of outcomes.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources are silent and adherents split.

civilizational-union.rationale: The tradition organizes politics by class and democracy rather than shared civilization, an inference.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The SEP entry stresses solidarity and community alongside equality, in opposition to the celebration of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Luxemburg defends individual freedom and political rights even against a revolutionary government, so community duties do not override rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not covered by the sources and adherents are divided.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Trotsky and the Marxist tradition regard industrial production as the material basis for socialism and wish to expand it democratically.

restore-past-order.rationale: Luxemburg holds that socialism must grow from living experience and be forward-looking, and the tradition aims at transformation rather than restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not directly addressed; adherents value empirical results but also hold firm to principles.

direct-action.rationale: Luxemburg wants mass action tied to elections and representative bodies, and the Wikipedia article's multi-party stance favours parliament alongside other action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Luxemburg argues that suppressing democracy during the revolution corrupts the socialism it aims to build, so means must embody the democratic ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Trotsky's argument that socialism builds on planned industrial production rules out a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The sources do not treat it as a programme; Trotsky sees socialist culture emerging over a long time, while Marx's aim appears in the wider tradition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Trotsky treats distribution by need as the long-run communist stage after the state dies away, though socialist democracy's programme concerns the earlier stage.

production-for-use.rationale: Trotsky's call for planning with a democracy of producers and consumers aims at production for need, while market socialists accept profit-seeking firms; adherents lean towards use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The SEP entry discusses exploitation accounts central to socialist critique, but it says there is no single account, and liberal socialists do not all hold the labor theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Luxemburg accepts the dictatorship of the class, exercised through full democracy, and Trotskyists keep the concept, while reformist democratic socialists in the scope reject it, so adherents are genuinely split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The sources do not take this up, and the strands differ between Marxists who agree and liberal socialists who do not.

taxation-theft.rationale: The SEP entry's whole case for socialism assumes democratic redistribution is legitimate, and taxation is a standard tool of this.

harm-principle.rationale: Luxemburg's freedom for dissent matches liberal limits on state power, but adherents also accept limits for economic and social ends.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The SEP entry stresses collective and social control of production and solidarity, while still respecting individual freedoms; the claim that only individuals have rights is rejected.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts the SEP's democratic-participation basis of socialist politics.

positive-liberty.rationale: The SEP entry's concern with equal access to the means of participating in decisions and with domination makes freedom depend on material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources attribute power to capitalists, not media and universities; adherents generally reject the premise.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The tradition rejects racial hierarchy and attributes differences to social conditions.

organic-representation.rationale: Socialist democracy relies on multi-party elections or direct democracy, not family or corporate representation in place of parties.

total-state.rationale: Luxemburg warns that bureaucratic state direction of life kills public life, and Trotsky wants the state to wither.

national-rebirth.rationale: The tradition is not oriented to national decadence and renewal, which is a nationalist theme.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nothing in the tradition supports expansion, which is seen as imperialist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on democratic consent, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Trotsky and the tradition aim at liberating labour from compulsion, and nothing supports bound farm labour.

universal-morality.rationale: The SEP entry shows socialists drawing on both liberal egalitarian universalism (Rawls, Mill) and Marxist historical views, so adherents split.

single-common-good.rationale: The tradition builds on competing class interests and democratic contestation, as in the SEP and Luxemburg, rather than a single reasoned good.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not covered, and adherents are split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The SEP entry says democratic socialists extend democratic principles to the workplace, and the Wikipedia article gives economic democracy through workers' control as part of the definition.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vouchers shift public provision to the market, against the SEP's emphasis on public provision and social ownership.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Wikipedia article's critics (Friedman) hold this claim and socialist democrats reject that socialism is incompatible with freedom, though some adherents accept a role for economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Luxemburg demands public control and democratic institutions, not moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not covered by the sources; Luxemburg actually criticised national self-determination, so the adherent view is a lean at best.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents are split between secular rationalism and religious socialists.

class-collaboration.rationale: Trotsky and Luxemburg rest on class conflict, and democratic socialists seek to remove the capitalist class, though reformists support bargaining.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Trotsky's culture argument treats inherited culture as foundation for socialist culture.

workers-nation.rationale: Trotsky's internationalism and the Fourth International's inclusion in the article show the working class as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The egalitarian tradition rejects legally distinct roles.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The SEP entry's egalitarian and anti-domination basis excludes legal racial classification and segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist strands in the article see the state as class rule, as Trotsky does for the bureaucratic caste; liberal socialists regard the democratic state as neutral, so it is a lean.

elite-replacement.rationale: The tradition rejects conspiracy theories about immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Wikipedia article names multi-party representative democracy, and Trotsky proposed electing a Soviet presidium by proportional representation, so proportionality is favoured.

national-mission.rationale: Exporting national government is a nationalist idea alien to the tradition.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Luxemburg warns of corruption without public control, but the statement's generalization is not a central position.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercive eugenics is incompatible with egalitarian democratic aims.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The SEP entry presents social ownership and democratic economic control as the programme, which a minimal state cannot deliver.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal moral worth is the basis of the egalitarian tradition, which excludes discouraging mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The SEP entry treats equal access to participation and equality as basic to socialism, though it does not use this wording.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Trotsky's permanent revolution says socialism needs international revolution, but reformist adherents do not hold this, so the current is split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not covered, and adherents are split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Luxemburg's freedom of thought excludes restricting religious choice.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A sectarian ban has no basis in the sources and conflicts with secular democratic lawmaking.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Trotsky says the state should wither and blames bureaucratic growth, and the article distinguishes this from Marxist-Leninist practice, so strengthening the state is rejected.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Luxemburg holds that socialism must rest on the active participation of the masses, with general elections and public control, which makes consent the source of legitimacy.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring minorities to leave contradicts the equal moral worth and democratic basis described in the SEP entry.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Trotsky accepts revolutionary force against the bureaucracy and the tradition rejects absolute libertarian non-aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The SEP stresses solidarity and criticises capitalist competition's inequalities.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Luxemburg demands freedom for those who think differently, which opposes outlawing parties, though some adherents accept bans on anti-democratic ones.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The SEP entry lists domination as one account of exploitation and capitalist domination in firms is a theme, so adherents embrace it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Luxemburg rejects party dictatorship and the reformist adherents reject vanguardism, though Trotskyists in the current favour a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social institutions oriented to equal participation and reducing inequality put the poor first in the SEP account.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Wikipedia article lists democratic trade unions as a form of economic democracy and Trotsky demands unions be revived, so restrictions on strikes are rejected.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The SEP entry attributes poverty to institutions and exploitation, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The tradition's solidarity rests on class and equal participation, not shared ethnicity, and the SEP entry's egalitarian grounds give no support to the claim that diversity weakens cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The SEP entry covers citizens' assemblies as part of socialist democracy but adherents mostly keep elections; sources show an openness without a clear position.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Luxemburg argues that suspending liberties in emergency leads to terror and bureaucratic rule.

party-controls-media.rationale: Luxemburg demands unrestricted freedom of the press, rejecting party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Luxemburg objects to party dictatorship over public life, which rules out party command of the army.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Paris Commune is cited in the article as a pre-Soviet example of socialist democracy, and workers' pay for officials is its known practice, though the article does not state the pay rule.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Luxemburg valued party discipline but opposed bureaucratic centralism, and adherents differ on binding members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Adherents are split between internationalist support and criticism of the EU as neoliberal.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentration of command in a head of state is contrary to democratic accountability in Luxemburg's analysis.

clerical-rule.rationale: Socialist democracy defines political authority through democratic institutions, not clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Trotskyists in the scope hold revolutionary defeatism, while democratic socialists and reformists reject it and Luxemburg opposed the war without adopting Lenin's defeatism, so adherents are split.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Luxemburg's freedom for those who think differently excludes censorship of art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Luxemburg demands public control and accountability, and unlimited tenure encourages the clique rule she condemns.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of delegates is characteristic of the Paris Commune and council forms in the article's examples; the article itself does not state the rule.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports banning rental, and social housing is the usual socialist alternative.

death-penalty.rationale: Luxemburg condemns rule by terror as demoralizing, and democratic socialist parties generally oppose capital punishment.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science-based public education is standard for the tradition.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Luxemburg's insistence on freedom for the one who thinks differently reflects Mill's argument, whom the article cites among liberal socialists.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not covered by the sources; adherents differ.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Luxemburg criticises Lenin and Trotsky for dissolving the elected Constituent Assembly and wants general elections, so she favours it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trotsky argues that Soviet democracy is needed for economic results and Stalin's authoritarianism hurt the five-year plan.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Democratic control of the economy contradicts insulating monetary policy from elected governments.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The SEP entry treats property forms as instruments for social ends, and the article gives social ownership as part of the definition.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Wikipedia article says Trotskyists call Soviet regimes degenerated workers' states, not state capitalist, while others in the current call them state capitalist, so adherents split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred divinely descended head of state is incompatible with democratic authority which defines socialist democracy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Flat taxation is contrary to the egalitarian redistributive aims of the SEP account.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Luxemburg demands public control and legal rights against rulers, which excludes a ruler above the law.

leader-cult.rationale: Trotsky attacks Stalin's personification of the bureaucracy, and the Wikipedia article contrasts socialist democracy with such regimes.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Trotsky holds that the bureaucracy can restore capitalism, supporting this, while reformists reject it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The tradition's class internationalism rejects ethnic territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Luxemburg's freedom for dissenting thought excludes punishing a change of religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress laws contradict the freedom Luxemburg defends and the equal citizenship of the tradition.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not a socialist aim; politics is organized by class and democracy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist strands in the article (Trotsky) hold this, while liberal socialists do not.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not covered; adherents split between letting banks fail and public takeover.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not a socialist aim and contrary to internationalism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Trotsky discusses material incentives under planning without moral incentives being a programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Luxemburg opposes putschism and relies on mass participation.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Democracy as the defining element rules out hereditary privilege.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Revolutionary adherents like Luxemburg and Trotsky expect crises, reformists believe in adaptation.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal moral worth and egalitarian aims in the SEP account point against a right to discriminate.

elective-rulers.rationale: The article defines socialist democracy through multi-party representative democracy, so rulers are chosen by election.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic decision-making binds minorities; this is an anarchist consensus idea the article ascribes to anarchists.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Luxemburg wanted representative bodies chosen by general election, while the councils strand wants councils; adherents split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Socialist democrats prefer rights and public provision to charity from privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Luxemburg insists that the masses must take part in public life, and socialist democracy depends on that participation.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal citizenship under democratic institutions leaves no ground for reserving offices to the native-born, which the sources never propose.

party-own-road.rationale: Trotsky criticises Moscow bureaucratic direction, and the article's party list includes independent parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The sources are about democracy within socialism, not development strategy, and adherents differ on aid and self-reliance.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Trotsky condemns Stalin's regime yet treats it as a deformed workers' state, so adherents oppose Stalinism but do not usually equate it with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Historical scholarship and the left's class and anti-slavery tradition treat slavery as the war's main cause, which adherents share.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The article presents democracy as a universal component of socialist schools, which points against claims that Western political institutions suit only some civilizations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Luxemburg treats rule by force and terror as demoralizing and wants public control, so a political guardian role for the army is rejected.

office-by-exam.rationale: Luxemburg rejects official decreeing, and the tradition favours elected offices.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private individual accounts replace social provision with market savings, against the SEP's social-ownership and equality aims.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not directly discussed; the socialist critique of capitalist acquisitiveness and the SEP's stress on solidarity lean toward agreeing.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Wikipedia article contrasts socialist democracy with Soviet-bloc practice; such intervention violates self-determination.

corporate-influence.rationale: The SEP entry says capitalists have disproportionate political influence.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The tradition rejects conspiracy theories against minorities as contrary to equal worth.

informal-organisation.rationale: The article contrasts socialist democracy's party, union and council structures with anarchist non-hierarchical alternatives.

religious-nation.rationale: A nation defined by religion cannot be squared with equal democratic citizenship in the article's meaning of socialist democracy.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Trotsky's internationalism and the equal-citizenship basis of the tradition have no place for tribute-based hierarchies of states.

defeat-communism.rationale: Trotsky defends nationalized property and planning against the bureaucracy, and the article lists communist parties among adherents, so adherents reject a campaign to defeat communism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist strands hold this while religious and liberal socialists do not, and the sources do not settle it.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Trotsky builds socialism on capitalism's productive basis.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not part of the tradition and clashes with its internationalism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The article lists cooperatives as forms of economic democracy, but not small property-sharing communities as a general social model.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement against minorities conflicts with equal citizenship and solidarity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Trotsky rejects both capitalism and bureaucratic rule, but the statement's third course is not a framing adherents use.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial has no place in the tradition, which rejects fascism and racism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminal penalties conflict with the equal moral worth and personal freedom the tradition upholds.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Luxemburg writes that freedom is freedom for the one who thinks differently and that suppressing public life produces terror and bureaucracy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Luxemburg's insistence on freedom for dissenting thought excludes penalties for blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The tradition's anti-imperialism opposes governing overseas territories for the ruling country's benefit.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Legitimacy under socialist democracy comes from democratic institutions, not religious conformity.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The SEP entry covers workplace democracy, participatory budgeting and deliberative democracy as socialist democracy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not in the chosen sources; modern adherent platforms accept it, and socialist feminism holds it.

assisted-dying.rationale: No position in the sources and adherents are split on the issue.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The SEP entry defines socialism through its distinct egalitarian and social-ownership commitments, so adherents see the left-right split as meaningful.

alienated-labor.rationale: The SEP entry treats worker self-management as a core ideal addressing domination and loss of control at work, though it does not use the alienation term here.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The statement is a cultural-prejudice claim, and the equal moral worth and pluralism of the tradition reject it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority in socialist democracy comes from democratic institutions, not from God.

social-market-economy.rationale: The SEP separates socialism from regulated capitalism: some adherents accept it as a stage, democratic socialists seek social ownership, so the current is split.

rich-first.rationale: Letting some grow rich first conflicts with the egalitarian focus on equal access to participation.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession conflicts with the elected offices of socialist democracy.

property-franchise.rationale: Luxemburg demands general elections with full participation, which rules out property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Eco-feminist socialists hold it while others do not.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The SEP entry argues that capitalist wealth distorts democracy, and the article's economic democracy aims to correct it, though neither speaks of the press specifically.

racial-franchise.rationale: Luxemburg's call for general elections and the equal citizenship of the tradition exclude racial restrictions.

open-government-data.rationale: Luxemburg insists on public control and an open public life as a safeguard against bureaucratic corruption.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The tradition's secular equal citizenship contradicts legal restrictions on interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority's shops contradicts equal moral worth and solidarity.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The SEP entry discusses citizens' assemblies as part of socialist democracy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Economic democracy through social ownership aims at rough equality of means, and the sources hold that concentrated private economic power undermines real political democracy.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Public provision and social ownership are listed as forms of economic democracy, so the state is expected to carry the main burden of helping the poor.

term-limits.rationale: Adherents are split; the Commune tradition favours recall and rotation, while the sources stress free elections without discussing term limits.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Socialist democracy rejects party dictatorship and demands free public life, which excludes state-drilled youth organisations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Social ownership and workers' control aim to end income from capital ownership, as the SEP account of socialism describes.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Socialist democracy treats politics as open public debate and class interest, not a spiritual contest between good and evil.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic democracy means control by workers and the public of all backgrounds, and the internationalist stance opposes ethnic economic reservation.

independent-unions.rationale: Socialist democracy envisages democratic unions and workers' control, and its adherents reject state or party control of working-class organisations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Luxemburg calls for the dictatorship of the class, not of a party, and the page states that socialism needs workers' self-rule through councils and unions.

person-over-state.rationale: Its rejection of one-party rule and suppression of dissent treats people as citizens with rights, not instruments of the state.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources are silent, and adherents are split between equal-treatment and distinct-values views.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Adherents are split: reformists accept a state monopoly of force while Trotskyists favour workers' militias; the sources do not settle it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Democratic unions are listed as an institution of economic democracy, and workers' bargaining power is central to the strand.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Genuinely split: Trotskyists and Luxemburg's followers want soviet or council democracy, while reformists would use the elected state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Luxemburg insists socialism cannot be decreed from above and must grow from the experience of open public life, which rejects a fixed blueprint.

workers-own-party.rationale: Socialist democracy builds on workers' councils, unions and socialist parties as vehicles of working-class self-rule, though it also stresses pluralism of parties.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The article holds that political democracy must be complemented by economic democracy, so elections alone do not suffice.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Luxemburg and Trotsky demand free press, assembly and open public life, and reject suppression of dissent, which a shutdown would be.

women-suffrage.rationale: Luxemburg's critique of Bolshevism demands universal suffrage and full political rights for the people.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Socialists often link religion to oppression but many adherents stress class over religion; the sources do not settle it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Trotsky's account defends the nationalised economy against restoration even under bureaucracy, but democratic socialists and Luxemburg's heirs reject the premise, so the strands are split.

indirect-election.rationale: Soviet or council democracy chose delegates upward, as Trotsky wanted, but multi-party direct elections are equally central, so adherents are split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Luxemburg demands public control, free press and assembly, and rejects dictatorship and terror, which excludes killing suspects without trial.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Luxemburg insists on free elections, parties, press and assembly as the means of public control, so bypassing them is rejected.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inherited from Marx and Trotsky, who treat labour as the source of value, but reformist adherents are split on its relevance.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Luxemburg rejects party dictatorship, and the scope excludes the Marxist-Leninist sense of the term, so communist-party rule is rejected.

missingStatements.text: Socialism should be introduced only with the freely expressed consent of a majority of the people.
missingStatements.rationale: Luxemburg holds that socialism needs the active participation of the masses and cannot be decreed by a party, and the article defines socialist democracy by popular democratic control.

missingStatements.text: Freedom of the press and of assembly should be guaranteed for opponents of the government as well as its supporters.
missingStatements.rationale: Luxemburg states that freedom is always for the one who thinks differently and that without unrestricted press and assembly public life dies out.

notes: The label is claimed by Marxist-Leninist states for one-party rule; this profile follows the democratic strand and would answer one-party, media-control and opposition questions oppositely for the Marxist-Leninist usage. It overlaps heavily with democratic socialism. Most non-core answers are low-confidence inferences.
